title: Normalized completed-linear compact-support scalar arrow
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $D$ with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-pur-conventions], finite extensions $E,F/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra embedding $i:E\to F$, and $e\ge1$ with $\varpi_E\mathcal O_F=\varpi_F^e\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with supplied compactification $c=(j,p_c)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the completed coefficient systems, their ordinary derived scalar extension $C_W=-\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$, and the canonical proper/open scalar comparisons of [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. Choose the normalized coefficient derived-system calculi $S_E,S_F$ on $X$ [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. For $H=E,F$ let $P_H^c$ be the total derived inverse limit of the separately derived native proper/open quotient system; write $\operatorname{Res}_H$ for exact restriction to constant integral coefficients, $U_H^c$ for the constant strict support system, and $\sigma_H:\operatorname{Res}_H P_H^c\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim U_H^c$ for its canonical identification [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-maps]. Let $M$ be complete bounded constructible with one uniform finite-Tor interval for every positive reduction [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $a_M^c=r_e^{-1}R\varprojlim(q_M^c)\tau$ for the normalized strict scalar-limit arrow and $\chi$ for the canonical pure-tensor comparison between constant and completed scalar restriction [lem-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-reduction]. Define the completed-linear compact-support scalar arrow $\gamma_M^c:C_YP_E^cM\to P_F^cC_XM$ to be the unique arrow satisfying
$$\sigma_F\circ\operatorname{Res}_F(\gamma_M^c)\circ\chi_{P_E^cM}=a_M^c\circ T_0(\sigma_E).$$
The construction retains its uniqueness helper: the type of arrows satisfying this exact normalization has exactly one element. The selected map is the existing normalized completed-linear lift, not an arbitrary morphism with the same endpoints, and no scalar-composition theorem is asserted.
